about: World generation and world content catalog. Read by UF_WorldGen, UF_Tiles, UF_Objects, UF_Items, UF_Jobs, UF_Wildlife, UF_History, UF_Colonists, UF_Factions, UF_Stance, UF_Look. Art and content are added here without touching code: docs/design/WORLD_ARCHITECTURE.md (schema), docs/handoffs/HANDOFF_world_generation.md (how to add an object), docs/ASSET_INVENTORY.md (every asset in use and its status). The world is one surface layer (the underground layer was removed 2026-09-18). Owner: Claude Code; Gemini may edit objects, items.types, wildlife.species and people only.

tilesets.about: Runtime tileset built by UF_Tiles (ID 91). A2 = ground kinds drawn in code (UF_GenGround_A2, same order as groundKinds). Flags are copied from the 'base' editor tileset. Replace a name here when art arrives (AR-100/AR-101).

water.about: Water kinds by A1 autotile ID (edges computed by the engine) in tilesets.surface.A1. Stock RMMZ sheet until AR-101.

climate.about: World fields in 0-1 from the seed, like DF's world map with its standard settings: elevation (with an ocean rim around the world), rainfall, temperature (north is colder, high ground is colder), drainage, volcanism, savagery, alignment. docs/design/WORLD_ARCHITECTURE.md section 3 turns them into biomes.

biomes.about: Every DF surface biome. ground = groundKinds id; water = key in water.surface; plants = object id -> chance per cell (0-1). Wildlife per biome is in wildlife.species[].biomes.

regions.about: Region character from the savagery and alignment fields (DF's savagery and good/evil). Cursed and blessed swap ground kinds and add plants; savagery scales wildlife and monsters (wildlife.savageryScale).

start.about: The start (VISION V4, revised again 2026-09-18): the player's faction's home site stands at the map centre (UF_History), and its people there are the colonists (UF_Colonists); there is no fixed pair any more. 'pair' is kept for reference only (its tiers are the human clothing-tier walk sheets: 0 naked, 1 fiber wraps, 2 hides, 3 tailored, used for human colonists by gender). 'names' are the syllables for people's names. The centre is always habitable (climate.startClimate) and gets the kit below within reach.

pond.about: A pond at a random direction and distance from the start, so the pair can drink.

kit.about: V67 (user 2026-09-19): every faction's area holds, within radius[1] cells of its campfire, what its band needs for its first buildings, tools, clothes and meals, whatever the biome rolled. UF_WorldGen places what the generator left short on free land in the ring radius[0]..radius[1] (never on a camp: its disc is kept clear). objects: the minimum count of each object within radius[1]. ore: an ore outcrop, one of ids, count pieces (id and count seeded per area). nearWater: ids placed within 3 cells of water when the ring has such cells. firstStage: the colony-plan steps whose materials the kit must cover (UF.WorldGen.kitNeeds adds them up for every culture: 8 founders, the standing campfire counts as the hearth, mealsPerFounder food items on top of the plan's food step); the worldgen kit_covers_plan check compares them with what the objects within radius[1] yield. water: UF_Factions places each area where drinkable water (these kinds) lies within reach cells of its centre when the map has such a place. wildlife: UF_Wildlife's prey herds for every campfire.

ore.about: V67: an ore outcrop within reach of every campfire (mined for ore and a stone; it leaves loose stones).

firstStage.about: Sizing the kit (2026-09-19): the plan steps that give the band its first buildings (larder, woodpile, shelter, beds, the workshop plan's workstone; the hearth is the standing campfire), tools (knives each, an axe, a pick), clothes (a fiber wrap each) and meals (the food step). Hide cloaks, tanning and everything after need hunting and workshops and are not part of it. The most any culture needs, 8 founders (2026-09-19 catalog): 16 logs, 40 stones (dwarf and automaton stone walls), 58 fiber (8 wraps of 6, 8 knives, axe, pick), 6 straw (the forest plan's 3 straw beds), 16 food (the forest plan's 8 in the larder plus a meal each). The kit's minimums alone are worth 36 logs (oaks 4 each with the stump, the fruit tree 4), 44 stones (+3 per ore outcrop), 60 fiber, 8 straw, 19 food.

water.about: Drinkable water within reach of every area centre (UF_Factions prefers such places; the worldgen kit_per_area check reports each area's nearest).

wildlife.about: V67 (2026-09-19): for every faction's campfire, one herd per group (a seeded pick among the group's species that live in the camp's biome, count members) at distance cells in a seeded direction, within the colonists' hunt radius (colony.huntRadius); no predator or monster placed within predatorFree cells of any campfire.

mapKit.about: Whatever the seed rolled, the whole map should hold what a colony needs (user rule 2026-09-18, like a DF site with all its layers). Minimum object counts over the map; a missing class gets small seeded patches (patchSize each) at least keepAway cells from the start, on the ground kinds listed first, else anywhere on land. Not placed by UF_WorldGen yet (2026-09-19: only start.kit is placed, around every faction area); UF_Roads reads these minimums so its roads never clear an object class below them.

water.about: At least this many fresh-water cells on the map; the start pond and rivers normally provide them.

rivers.about: Rivers run north-south through the whole world at random places each game, never through the start, and stop where the ocean begins.

items.about: Things that lie on the ground, get carried and stored (UF_Items). image = character sheet drawn at the cell (stand-ins !$U7_Item_* until AR-200 originals). food.hunger = hunger removed when eaten. tool = what jobs it speeds up (skill multiplier); wear = clothing tier it gives when equipped.

materials.about: Materials of made things (docs/design/COMBAT_CHAINS.md section 1). kind = the family; density in kg per litre; hardness 0-10; value = worth per unit for trade later; damage / armor = multipliers UF_Combat applies to a weapon's rolled dice (melee: the weapon's material; ranged: the ammunition's) and to an armor piece's ac bonus, rounded half up, minimum 1 damage on a hit. Bronze has no recipe until a tin ore exists; the row fixes its numbers. Written 2026-09-18 (Claude Code).

recipes.about: Things colonists make by hand (UF_Jobs 'craft'): inputs from the crafter's inventory, outputs given to the crafter. at = an object tag the crafter must stand next to (null = anywhere). tool = a tool tag that speeds it up (never required). User request 2026-09-18: clothes, tools, cooking from day one. Combat-chain recipes (2026-09-18 night, docs/design/COMBAT_CHAINS.md) carry at (workshop tag), labor, skill, ability (the quality roll's ability), material (of the output) and quality (rolled at craft); their work is in beats (6-12, WORLD_ARCHITECTURE section 1.7) while the older recipes above them are still in ticks until the beat integration rescales them.

labors.about: Labors that run the combat chains (VISION V43 and V55; docs/design/COMBAT_CHAINS.md section 6). jobs = the job types the labor covers; skill = the colony.skills entry it trains and that its quality rolls use; priority = the cultures.<species>.priorities key it inherits, multiplied by cultures.<species>.chainWeights[labor]. The full labor set (mining, woodcutting, ...) arrives with the labors build; these are the ones the chain recipes and the arming step name. Written 2026-09-18 (Claude Code).

sites.about: Layouts of faction sites and ruins (object ids from 'objects'). ring = object around the site at 'radius' with 'gaps' openings; center = object in the middle; inside = objects scattered inside. kinds by species: index by how big the site grew (population thresholds in 'growth'). Since 2026-09-19 (VISION V31: no history) a New Game stamps none of them: each faction gets one bare record of kind founding.kind at its area centre (no pieces; UF_WorldGen only keeps its disc, radius + 1, free of plants), and whatever the bands build comes from play. The layouts are still used by the older history generator (history.simulate) and by saves made before 2026-09-19.

founding.about: The record each faction's area gets at New Game (UF_History): a site of this kind with stamp false (nothing placed), used for its name, its radius (the clearing and the colony's plan cells) and the look label.

preferredBiomes.about: History looks for a site cell in one of these biomes first (any walkable land if none is found in the home area).

wildlife.about: Creatures placed with the map on New Game (UF_Wildlife), as world units that live on and off screen. herds per area per species = weight in 'biomes' x savageryScale x (herd count roll). Stand-in images are U7 sheets (AR-401) with a tint for variants; minSavagery/alignment restrict monsters to wild or cursed regions. kind: grazer/vermin/flier = prey (hunt yields 'yields'), predator/monster = dangerous (hunted only with a knife and bravery, UF_Colonists).

people.about: Walk sheets for faction members by species (UF_History spawns them at sites; UF_Wildlife's wander AI moves them). U7 stand-ins until AR-400; tints tell species apart on shared sheets. stats = per-score modifiers (str, dex, con, int, wis, cha) added to the d20 ability scores UF_History rolls for each person (VISION V53); missing keys are 0.

factions.about: Factions are rolled from the world seed on every New Game (UF_Factions): 4-7 of them, species by weight, stances, relations from -100 (at war) to +100 (allied). One of them, of a species with playable != false, is the player's (factions.playerId). User decision 2026-09-19 (VISION V4, V31): no history; every faction gets its own area (areas) on habitable land and starts there as founders (founders) with nothing built. Species are generic placeholders (VISION V7-V9); rename or replace them freely.

areas.about: Where each faction's area centre goes (UF_Factions, seeded): on walkable land (no water, no peak rock, no cursed region unless the species is in cursedOk) whose disc of clearDisc cells is walkable too; the player's within playerReach cells of the map centre (the habitable start); every other at least minGap cells from every centre and edgeMargin cells from the map edge, in one of sites.preferredBiomes[species] with drinkable water within start.kit.water.reach when the map has such a place.

founders.about: Every faction starts as this many men and women (VISION V4; eight founders around a lit campfire, user 2026-09-19 afternoon), adults aged within age, on free cells within reach cells of its area centre (UF_History). One of them leads the band (rank 1, a title from titles); the others answer to the leader (VISION V52). Names from people[species].names when a species has its own table, else start.names; stats rolled per VISION V53.

history.about: The world's chronicle (UF_History). User decision 2026-09-19 (VISION V4, V31 revised, V54 retired): no history at New Game. Every faction starts in year 1 as four founders (factions.founders) in its own area (factions.areas), with nothing built; the chronicle opens with one Year 1 line per faction and then records what happens in play (UF.History.addEvent). simulate = false and settleYears = 0 switch off the older generator that UF_History keeps (500-600 simulated years of sites, wars and ruins, then the settling run on the built map); the keys after settleYears are that generator's tunables, unused while simulate is false. titles: the older generator's ruler titles.

settle.about: The settling run (UF_History, VISION V54): the last settleYears of the history played out on the built map, site by site, before the people are spawned. Tunables (defaults in UF_History when missing): birthChancePerPair per adult pair per year, feverChancePerYear and feverLoss, peoplePerHouse / peoplePerBed / peoplePerStockpile / workbenchAt thresholds, secondWallAt (fraction of the site capacity), treesPerPersonYear / stonesPerPersonYear / bushesPerPerson and depleteFraction (at most this share of what stands within radius + reach), minPeople (fewer and a site is abandoned).

colony.about: UF_Colonists: needs per game minute, thresholds that trigger need jobs, sleeping hours, personality facets, and the society plan every faction's band follows without orders (VISION V17, V21, V51: built and made one piece at a time at its own camp). plan steps: build = an object on cells relative to the camp's centre; craft = a recipe until each member has (equip) or the band holds (count) the item; stock = keep this many food items in the larder (hunting or gathering); society = shelter or beds marks a step UF_Society owns when that plugin is loaded (its rooms give the step's status and the band doesn't build it itself).

plans.about: Plan variants by culture (cultures.<species>.plan names one; 'default' = colony.plan); every faction's band follows its species' variant. Cells are relative to the camp's centre; a cell that already holds the same object counts as done, a cell holding another building is skipped.

combat.about: Combat in the OSRS model (VISION V64, user 2026-09-19; the d20 rules of V47 are retired). UF_Combat, docs/systems/UF_Combat.md. Real time on the map in ticks of tickFrames map updates (36 = 0.6 s at x1; the speed keys play more map updates per frame, so ticks speed up with them). Per attack: effective level = level + the style's bonus + levelOffset; max attack roll A = effective attack (ranged, magic) x (the equipment's attack bonus for the attack type + 64); max defence roll D = effective defence x (the defence bonus for that type + 64); against magic a person's effective defence is floor(magicDefence.magic x magic) + floor(magicDefence.defence x (defence + style bonus)) + levelOffset and a creature's is magic + style bonus + levelOffset; both rolls are seeded uniform integers 0..A and 0..D and the attack hits when its roll is higher, so hit chance = 1 - (D + 2) / (2 (A + 1)) when A > D, else A / (2 (D + 1)); max hit = floor(0.5 + effective strength x (strength bonus + 64) / 640) (ranged: effective ranged and ranged strength, magic: effective magic and magic strength) + a creature's maxHitBonus; a hit deals a seeded uniform 0..max hit, capped at the target's hitpoints. styles: level bonuses (accuracy = the attack, ranged or magic level used; strength; defence), speed = ticks added to the weapon's attack speed, range = cells added. Creatures fight in creatureStyle with wildlife.species[].combat and never level up; people read UF.Skills levels, else unit.data.combatLevels, else the people levels here (hitpoints 10), else 1. Maximum hitpoints = the hitpoints level. modes (VISION V29) = unit.data.combat.mode; defaultModes by unit: hostile, fleeing prey (hunt.flees), everyone else. aggroRadius, leash and fleeRadius in cells. regen: hitpoints back per everyTicks (100 ticks = 60 s at x1 = one game hour on the clock). display: hitsplat life and the health bar's hide delay in real milliseconds (interface, not simulation; 1 s and 6 s). quality (crafting, phase 2 of docs/design/COMBAT_CHAINS.md): an item record's quality 0-5 comes from UF.Skills.qualityRoll at craft (VISION V63); names for the sheet and the look label; bonus multiplies the item's bonuses; value for trade. Written 2026-09-19 (Claude Code).

cultures.about: Per-species culture (user decision 2026-09-18): each faction's build style, people and priorities. wall/ring = the pieces its sites and colonists build with (sites.bySpecies gives the site kinds); priorities = multipliers the colonists' planner applies when choosing work (job types); facetBias = added to seeded personality facets; plan = which colony plan variant (colony.plans key, or 'default'); tint = the people sheet tint (people.<species>). Culture names are generic; no invented lore.

stance.about: Colored squares under units' feet (UF_Stance; user request 2026-09-18): green = friendly (your colony and allied factions), yellow = indifferent (wildlife, neutral factions), red = hostile (monsters, factions at war).

arrivals.about: Groups that arrive from the map edges (UF_Arrivals; VISION V19). One seeded roll per game day for every faction that has a living site; the faction's relation to the player's picks the kind: allied/friendly -> settlers (migrants) and traders, neutral -> travellers (wanderers), hostile/war -> raiders. The player's own faction sends settlers when it has another living site. Chances are per day per faction and are multiplied by the season. Sizes are [min, max] people. Every group lands on the coast nearest the faction's home (the map's rim is ocean), walks in, and leaves the way it came.

migrants.name: settlers
migrants.bark: We have come to join you.

traders.name: traders
traders.bark: Goods from afar, come and see.
traders.announce: A caravan of {faction} arrives from the {edge}.

wanderers.name: travellers
wanderers.announce: {n} travellers of {faction} pass by from the {edge}.

goods.about: Trade goods by the trading faction's species: [itemId, [min, max]] per stack; goodsPerTrader stacks per trader; `default` when the species has no list. Item ids must exist in items.types.

anim.about: Combat and death animations (UF_Anim, VISION V58). remainsHours: game hours a dead creature's remains lie on its cell (they fade over the last hour). Death, attack and hurt frames come from each sheet's sidecar (animations.dead, attack, hurt; ASSET_REQUESTS AR-600).

sheet.about: The selection panel (UF_Sheet; VISION V59, V49; user 2026-09-19). grid: the inventory grid, columns x rows of slot x slot px. slots: the equipment slots in order. slotAliases: older unit.data.equipment keys shown in a slot until every reader moves to the five slots (tool = weapon, clothes = torso). faces: placeholder portraits per species id (people and wildlife) and gender key (male, female, <stage>_<gender> such as elder_male, any) as [faceSheet, index] pairs from img/faces (stock RPG Maker sheets, 4 columns x 2 rows of 144x144) until AR-700; the pick is stable per unit (unit id modulo the list); a species with no usable entry gets the code-drawn UF_GenFace silhouette. unit.data.face { sheet, index } overrides. Owner: Claude Code.

fire.about: UF_Fire (docs/systems/UF_Fire.md): fire is a cell state that spreads (VISION V21, V25). Times are beats (1 beat = beatFrames map updates, 60 = one per second at x1; UF.Beat when it exists). Every beat each burning cell rolls (seeded: world seed, beat, cell, direction) to ignite each of its 4 neighbours with the neighbour's `spread` chance and spends 1 beat of its `burn` fuel; when the fuel is gone the object becomes `becomes` (null = nothing), the ground kind becomes `ground` when given, and items on the cell are destroyed when `destroysItems`. Doused (water) objects become `dousedBecomes` when given. The first rule whose `ids` holds the object id, or whose `tags` are all on the object, decides; `never` = does not burn; objects no rule matches never burn. `source` objects (campfires) never burn: each beat each flammable 4-neighbour catches with `escapeChance`. `flame`: "tall" draws the taller flame sprite. startChance = chance per beat of an accidental start on a random cell of the area on screen (0 = off). damage = hit points lost per beat by a unit standing in fire. douse: fires within campRadius of the player's camp get open douse jobs (at most maxOpen at once) when water is within waterRadius of the fire; fillBeats at the water, beats at the fire; a doused cell can't catch for wetBeats.

talk.about: Conversations (UF_Talk, VISION V25; added 2026-09-19): keyword talks with any person, in the manner of the classic keyword conversations. Every line is a template below filled from the simulation: {slot} values are names and facts read from the world state, and a slot that names a person, faction or place adds that keyword to the talk. A section's variants are tried most specific first; a template whose slots are unknown is skipped. kinds = unit kinds that can talk. portraits = stock RPG Maker face placeholders by species > gender > stage ("Sheet:index"), used until the AR-700 face sets exist (catalog.faces or unit data.face win when present); species without an entry get a code-drawn UF_GenFace. Original generic wording only: no proper nouns. Layout (VISION V62, 2026-09-19): the person's portrait with their words a page at a time (words.more marks a page with more after it), the portrait of whoever speaks for you beside the keywords, and chime = what your people standing near the person may add with their own portrait.

chime.about: What your people standing near the person say (UF_Talk, VISION V62, 2026-09-19): after each line, the nearest of yours within range cells (not the person, not whoever speaks for you, not a baby) who has something to say chimes in with their own portrait and line. named: the line names them; self: the topic is them; partner, child, mother, father: the topic is that relative of theirs; factionGood, factionBad: the topic is a faction yours is allied or friendly with, or hostile to or at war with; greetFriendly, greetWary: a stranger's greeting, and news: the news, these three only by chance percent (seeded). Never on bye, never in a hostile or baby talk. Slots: {name} the companion, {speaker} the person spoken to, {person}, {faction}.

factionGood: {faction} have always been fair with us.

portraits.about: Stock RPG Maker face placeholders (img/faces, 4 x 2 cells of 144 x 144, index 0-7 row by row) until AR-700. Species > gender > stage; a missing stage falls back to adult (baby to child).

lines.about: Conversation lines for the U7-model talk (VISION V62 revised 2026-09-19, V65 tone; added 2026-09-19). UF_Talk reads a section here first and falls back to the same section at the top of "talk" (the older keys stay readable). {slot} = a name or fact from the simulation (a slot that names a person, faction or place adds that keyword). [topic] or [words|topic] = a topic word: the words are written into the line and the topic joins the player's keyword list (family, home, mood, others, news, need = the speaker's most pressing need, labelled by needWords). A template whose slots or topics the speaker has nothing on is skipped. Plain generic wording only: no proper nouns.

chime.about: Companions within range cells of the person spoken to (the player's colonists, not the player's own portrait, not babies or small children). After an answer (or a greeting), first the nearest one the answer concerns speaks, from talk.chime (the line names them, the topic is them or their kin, or a faction they love or hate); otherwise, now and then (chance percent, seeded by the world, the person, the keyword and how often it was asked), one of them makes a remark from the lists here: the topic first, then the person's stance (own, friendly, wary), then any. {speaker} = the person spoken to, {name} = the companion (the same slots as talk.chime).

ambient.about: What moves on its own (UF_Ambient, VISION V60, ART_STANDARD U8). objects: rules tried in order; a rule matches an object type when its id is in ids or any of its tags is in tags, and the first match picks the motion: sway and ripple (the sprite shears from its foot; amp = how far its top moves, in pixels at zoom 1; period in frames, 60 = 1 s, one value per object from hash32 of its cell and type), fire (flame overlay, flicker, smoke puffs rising smokeRise px over smokeLife frames, one every smokeEvery frames; flameAt = where the flame's foot sits, from the object's anchor), door (an in-between frame while a UF_Doors door opens or closes), still. work: bob or spark while a job at the object is in its work state. A sheet whose sidecar names frames under animations (sway, idle, lit, work, open) steps those frames at frameMs instead of the code motion. Types no rule matches stay still. creatures: breathing (amp px, period frames, starts after frames of standing), idle turns (after idle frames, then every), fliers (units with one of these tags) bob amp px. water: glints on water cells in view by day (at most max, one per cellsPerGlint water cells, life frames each, gap frames between). particles: leaves over leaf grounds, pollen over pollen grounds, at most max on screen, one every frames. houses: chimney smoke over rooms UF_Society lists as lived in or with a lit hearth.

skills.about: Skills that grow by doing (VISION V63, V64; UF_Skills, docs/systems/UF_Skills.md; written 2026-09-19 by Claude Code). Levels 1-99; xp for level L = floor(sum over i = 1..L-1 of floor(i + 300 * 2^(i/7)) / 4): level 2 = 83, 10 = 1154, 50 = 101333, 92 = 6517253, 99 = 13034431; xp stops at maxXp. list: kind trade or combat; jobs = the job types whose jobs:done trains it (hunting is trained by jobs:kill); recipeSkills / recipeAt = the craft recipes it covers (recipes.list[].skill, then .at; any other recipe trains the skill with craftDefault); buildTags = a build job of an object with one of these tags also gives this skill xp.buildShare of the building xp; xp = { base, perWork }: one job gives base + perWork x min(the job's work in ticks, xp.workCap). noSkill = job types that train nothing. effects: work rate x (1 + (level - 1) x speedPerLevel); extraYield: on jobs:done of these job types a seeded chance of level x chancePerLevel of one more of the first yield on the job's cell; quality (0-max) = floor((level - 1) x perLevel + roll x spread). combatXp: xp per damage point dealt, by attack type (melee = stab, slash, crush) and style, plus hitpointsPerDamage. start: starting levels when a person appears, by life stage (stageAges, else defaultStage), species (favoured skills roll twice and keep the higher) and culture (a trade's weight = tradeWeight x (the culture's highest priority among the trade's jobs, or craft for recipe skills, x its highest chainWeight among the labors that train it) ^ cultureExponent). oldRecord: a data.skills record (0-20) from a save made before skills becomes levels 1 + round(points x levelPerPoint). chronicle: milestone levels written to the chronicle, and the line when someone whose total level is above deathMinTotal dies. speech: the line shown over the head at a level-up.

speech.about: Over-head speech (UF_Speech, VISION V62; added 2026-09-19): remarks, barks, shouts, orders and thoughts float as plain text above the speaker's head, follow them and fade; no bubble, no box. Text is the game font at fontSize px with an outline of outlineWidth (RMMZ's canvas stroke width, centred on the letter edge) in outlineColor, rows lineHeight px apart, at most maxChars characters a row and maxLines rows a line; longer text becomes consecutive lines by the same speaker, in order. A line lasts framesBase + framesPerChar x its characters frames (at most framesMax) unless the caller gives frames; frames are 1/60 s at every game speed and stop while the game is paused. fadeIn/fadeOut: frames. gap: px between the head and the text; spacing: px kept between two lines that would overlap (the later line moves up). maxOnScreen: lines shown at once (the oldest bark gives way first, else the oldest line); maxQueue: lines one speaker keeps waiting. minZoom: below this map zoom no text is shown (the text keeps its screen size at every zoom). headDefault: px above the feet when a speaker's sprite size is unknown. routeBarks: UF_Visuals' barks are drawn by UF_Speech (false = UF_Visuals' own bubble, which fails in this NW.js build for want of the canvas roundRect, so no bark shows). kinds: colour per kind, optional bold/italic. Owner: Claude Code.

skins.about: Window skins per culture (UF_Factions; VISION V99, user 2026-09-19 14:42: "Every faction should have a different menu skin"). Every window of the player (every Window_Base) loads the skin of the player's faction's culture (faction.culture, else its species): img/system/<file>.png when that file exists, else a stand-in built once from img/system/<base>.png with the culture's recipe. A conversation (UF_Talk) draws each side's skin frame around that side's portrait: the stranger's side in the stranger's skin. recipe: a gradient map by brightness; back = [dark, mid, light] for the two wallpaper parts (x 0-95), frame = [dark, mid, light] for the frame, cursor, arrows and pause sign; mix = share of the original colour kept (0-1). The text colour row (x 96-191, y 144-191) is never changed, so text colours stay as Window.png has them (ColorManager reads Window.png). recipe null = <base> as it is. like = use another culture's entry. default = a culture without an entry. material = what Gemini's skin is made of (ASSET_REQUESTS AR-1700 to AR-1710, docs/handoffs/HANDOFF_skins_faces.md). Owner: Claude Code.

faces.about: Portraits per culture (VISION V100, user 2026-09-19 14:44: "Every faction should have it's own U7 faceset style"; V49, V62). Read by UF_Factions (cultureFace, faceStyle, drawPortrait) for UF_Talk's portraitOf and UF_Sheet's faceSpecOf. A person's portrait, in order: unit data.face (an explicit face); the sheets of the person's culture (faction.culture, else the faction's species, else the unit's species): img/faces/<pattern> with {culture} the culture id and {n} 1 to sheets, used only for that culture's own people (its id, or its species list); then that people's species sheets (species.<species>.<gender>.<adult|elder>: sheet, indices, content = the content-mood cells, framed = the art has its own frame); then the portrait chosen before (catalog sheet.faces, talk.portraits, the code-drawn UF_GenFace) drawn inside a code-drawn frame in the culture's colours (cultures.<id>.standIn), so factions already look different before the art arrives. A species sheet with framed false gets the same code-drawn frame around it. Culture sheets: 576 x 288 RMMZ face sheets, eight 144 x 144 faces; layout = the cell of each adult and elder man and woman in the calm top row; the row below holds the same four faces content (contentMoods = unit moods that pick the lower row). Babies and children keep the chain's older portraits (framed). Creatures get no frame. cultures.<id>: frame, background, palette, motifs = Gemini's brief (ASSET_REQUESTS AR-1720 to AR-1730, docs/handoffs/HANDOFF_skins_faces.md); species = the peoples whose faces the culture's sheets show; like = another culture's entry; default = a person whose culture has no entry. standIn: shape of the opening (square, arch, pointed, round, notched, blob, cave), ornament (studs, leaves, ticks, teeth, stitches, knobs, diamonds, veins, bars, beads, none), thickness (share of the side), colors (frame, light, dark, back). Owner: Claude Code.

groundShades.about: VISION V93, docs/design/GROUND_SHADES.md: rolling terrain shades and gradient ramps across all overworld and subterranean biomes.

ecology.about: UF_Ecology (VISION V74, V75, V83, V85; docs/design/ECOLOGY.md, docs/systems/UF_Ecology.md): a census per (level, 64x64 block, biome) bucket; fauna breed near their herds and arrive from the map edge; monsters come on a seeded clock away from camps, sites and people; plants spread, seed and regrow on the same cell; minerals never return. The director runs once per game hour and services bucketsPerStep buckets in a seeded round-robin, never placing anything in view or on a cell a unit could not walk onto (V68). Every duration is in world beats. Owner: Claude Code.
